title: How we know
lede: What Lake Watch is built from, how it decides each lake's status, how it compares with optical images, and where it falls short.
can: NISAR made {cloud_looks} valid looks across {cloud_lakes} of {lake_count} lakes between {cloud_start} and {cloud_end}, the weeks when SUPARCO's updates reported cloud limiting optical imagery.
Each lake gets one plain status from its own earlier passes on the same viewing track, with the noise it was judged against shown beside it.
Passes that look wrong for their track (too bright, too dark, or outliers) are left out and listed with their reason, never read as growth or shrinkage.
cannot: Map a lake's exact shoreline. Against Sentinel-2, radar water {optical_overlap}, one date per lake.
See water hidden in radar shadow, frozen lakes, lakes under 0.05 km² or wind-roughened water reliably.
Say when or whether a lake will burst, or warn anyone. Lake Watch is indicative screening on provisional data, not an official warning service.

sections.title: Lake method
paragraphs: Lake Watch reads NISAR GCOV passes, HH and HV, from {cloud_start} on: NASA's provisional release (P05023) for passes up to 21 Oct 2026 and NASA's standard GCOV product (P05036) for later ones; this build uses {processing_versions}. Calibrated passes only, and one viewing track is never mixed with another. The cloud window for the headline count is {cloud_start} to {cloud_end}, while SUPARCO's 2 Jul and 5 Aug updates reported cloud limiting optical imagery. SUPARCO's 2 Jul update rests on one 16 Jun image; its 5 Aug update used images from 6 Jul to 5 Aug and reports 105 lakes unfrozen, up from 40 (space4climate.gov.pk, GLOF monitoring status 5 August 2026).

Water rule. A pixel is dark when both HH and HV are at least {drop_db} dB below the median of the search window in that pass. Each pass is first averaged over a {speckle_box} by {speckle_box} pixel box to calm speckle.

Two-view rule. A pixel is shadow-prone when it is dark in one viewing direction's season median image (ascending or descending) but not in the other's: that is radar shadow, not water. A single pass is then read as water when it is dark in that pass, inside the lake zone, not shadow-prone, and valid.

Each area is the water inside the lake's outline, buffered by 200 m, where it has one (from OpenStreetMap), and otherwise inside a search circle around its coordinates, 1 km unless the lake sets a smaller one for a small pond. A lake larger than its zone or its 6 km radar window is only partly counted, and lakes whose shores sit in radar shadow are underestimated. The data file's own note reads: "{notes}"
list: A pass whose window brightness is far from its own track's median is left out, listed on the lake with its reason, and never read as growth or shrinkage.

A pass is also left out when the share of dark pixels in its window, or its window-median HV, is an outlier among its own track's passes (robust z-score above {outlier_z}). The 5 Sep 2026 pass on track 156A, anomalous over the Hunza lakes, is left out by hand wherever this test does not already catch it; each lake lists the reason.
A trend needs at least {min_looks} valid looks from the same track. With fewer, the status is Not enough NISAR looks yet.
At least {min_observable_pct}% of the lake zone ({min_observable}) must be observable, not hidden by shadow or missing. Otherwise the status is Not observable, and no area is shown.

Noise is the spread of that lake's own pass-to-pass differences, never below {noise_floor_km2} km². A lake is Growing or Shrinking only when its latest area differs from the median of its earlier same-track looks by more than {change_factor} times that noise.
The status compares each lake only with its own earlier passes from the same track. A small change can move a label between passes, so read the numbers and their noise, not only the label.

sections.title: Sentinel-2 cross-check and what is not validated
paragraphs: Where a clear Sentinel-2 scene was close in time, we compared one NISAR pass with it inside each lake's zone (its outline where it has one, otherwise its search circle). Sites with no lake now are not compared. The rows below are copied from the data file.
afterTable: Radar water {optical_overlap}. Radar under-reads small lakes and loses water marked shadow-prone, and optical water misses shaded or very dark lakes, so neither is a clean reference.
This zone comparison is not a validation of lake extent. It compares two rough water maps of the same zone, on one date each.
The SUPARCO area comparison was skipped because no SUPARCO lake IDs or locations have been supplied.
Not validated: frozen lakes, lakes under 0.05 km², and wind-roughened water.

sections.title: The data
paragraphs: Lake Watch is built from public sources. Only the first two are satellite data.

head: Source
What we used it for
Status
rows: NISAR L2 GCOV, provisional and standard (NASA, from the ASF archive)
Every lake area and radar picture: HH and HV, every calibrated pass over each lake from 17 June 2026, {processing_versions}, read as a 6 km window per pass.

Passes up to 21 Oct 2026 are the provisional release (P05023): not validated, and NASA expects to reprocess it, so values may move. Later passes are NASA's standard GCOV product (P05036); we have seen no validation statement for it. A lake whose track spans both says so, because a calibration change can shift areas.
The optical cross-check: MNDWI water on a clear scene close in date to one NISAR pass.
Optical, so it fails under cloud; a rough reference, not ground truth.
The cloud window and the context: optical updates of 2 July and 5 August 2026.

sections.title: Limits
list: Areas are water inside a search zone, so a lake larger than its zone is only partly counted.
Radar pictures are NISAR GCOV crops on the UTM grid, north up; they are pictures, not interactive map overlays.
A status compares a lake only with its own earlier passes on one track; it is not an absolute size.
Passes up to 21 Oct 2026 are provisional NISAR data, subject to reprocessing; later passes are NASA's standard product, and a track that spans both can shift with the calibration change.

sections.title: Check it yourself
paragraphs: docs/DATA_SOURCES.md lists every source and its licence status. The pipeline in processing/ rebuilds every number on this page: lakes-search, lakes-fetch, lakes-build and lakes-check.
Not an official warning service. For warnings, use the Pakistan Meteorological Department, NDMA, GBDMA and PDMA.
